name: Paracetamol
summary: A common analgesic and antipyretic medicine used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever.
uses: Fever and chills
Headache and body ache
Dental pain
Muscle and joint aches
dosage: Adults: 500mg to 650mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 4,000mg in 24 hours.
sideEffects: Rare when taken at recommended doses
Nausea or stomach upset in sensitive individuals
Severe liver toxicity in cases of overdose
precautions: Avoid alcohol consumption while taking paracetamol to prevent liver strain
Do not combine with other medicines containing paracetamol/acetaminophen
Consult a doctor if fever persists for more than 3 consecutive days
howItWorks: Inhibits the production of prostaglandins in the central nervous system, reducing the sensation of pain and lowering the brain's temperature set-point.

name: Sunscreen (SPF 50+ PA++++)
genericName: Broad Spectrum UV Filters (Zinc Oxide, Titanium Dioxide, Bemotrizinol)
summary: A topical photoprotective product that absorbs or reflects sunlight ultraviolet (UVA/UVB) radiation.
uses: Prevention of sunburn and UV erythema
Protection against premature photoaging, wrinkles, and dark spots
Reduction of skin cancer risk (melanoma and carcinomas)
dosage: Apply approximately 2 finger-lengths generously to face and neck 15-20 minutes before sun exposure. Reapply every 2-3 hours.
sideEffects: Transient mild stinging around eyes
Occasional contact dermatitis or breakout if comedogenic
precautions: Reapply after sweating heavily or swimming
Pair with protective clothing and sunglasses during peak UV hours (10 AM - 4 PM)
Patch test before initial use if prone to allergic reactions
howItWorks: Forms a microscopic protective shield using physical blockers to deflect rays or chemical filters that absorb high-energy UV photons and convert them into harmless heat.

name: Salicylic Acid (2%)
summary: An oil-soluble beta hydroxy acid that deeply penetrates pores to exfoliate dead skin cells and clear trapped sebum.
uses: Acne vulgaris, whiteheads, and blackheads
Enlarged pores and excess sebum regulation
Mild keratosis pilaris and texture refinement
dosage: Apply 2-3 drops to cleansed, dry skin once every other evening initially, increasing to once daily as tolerated.
sideEffects: Mild skin dryness or flaking
Temporary tingling or mild erythema
Potential initial skin purging during weeks 1-3
precautions: Always follow with sunscreen during daytime as exfoliation increases photosensitivity
Avoid combining in the same routine with strong retinoids or direct vitamin C if skin is sensitive
Do not use if allergic to aspirin or other salicylates
howItWorks: Exerts keratolytic action by dissolving intercellular desmosomes that glue dead skin cells together, penetrating oily follicles to dissolve debris.

name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
genericName: Sodium Chloride, Potassium Chloride, Sodium Citrate & Dextrose
summary: A balanced electrolyte-glucose formulation recommended by the WHO to prevent and treat dehydration caused by illness.
uses: Dehydration resulting from acute diarrhea and vomiting
Heat exhaustion and heavy sweating after intense exertion
Restoration of fluid and electrolyte equilibrium in viral illnesses
dosage: Dissolve the standard packet (21.8g) into exactly 1 litre of clean drinking water. Sip in small quantities frequently.
sideEffects: Extremely safe with no common side effects when diluted accurately in the prescribed water volume
precautions: Do not add additional sugar, milk, or fruit juices to the rehydration mixture
Discard any reconstituted solution that has not been consumed within 24 hours
Patients with severe renal impairment should consume only under doctor supervision
howItWorks: Leverages the sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) in the intestinal mucosa, actively pulling water into the bloodstream even during gastrointestinal inflammation.

name: Niacinamide (5% - 10%)
summary: A potent water-soluble form of Vitamin B3 that fortifies skin barrier function, calms redness, and evens skin tone.
uses: Fading post-acne blemishes and hyperpigmentation
Strengthening the lipid barrier and reducing transepidermal water loss
Regulating sebum output and soothing inflammatory redness
dosage: Dispense 2-3 drops onto clean skin morning and evening before heavier moisturizers.
sideEffects: Rare mild flushing or sensitivity when starting with higher (10%) concentrations
precautions: Begin with a patch test on forearm before facial application
If burning occurs, dilute with a simple hyaluronic acid or gentle moisturizer
howItWorks: Serves as a precursor to cofactors NAD and NADP, stimulating ceramide synthesis in the epidermis and inhibiting melanosome transfer from melanocytes to keratinocytes.

name: Cetirizine Hydrochloride
summary: A second-generation non-sedating antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itching.
uses: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) and seasonal allergies
Chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives and itchy skin welts)
Allergic conjunctivitis (itchy, watery eyes)
dosage: Adults: One 10mg tablet once daily, preferably in the evening with or without food.
sideEffects: Mild drowsiness in approximately 10% of users
Dry mouth
Fatigue or mild headache
precautions: Caution when driving or operating heavy machinery until personal tolerance is known
Avoid combining with alcohol or central nervous system sedatives
howItWorks: Selectively antagonizes peripheral H1 histamine receptors, preventing histamine released by mast cells from triggering allergic reactions.

name: Ibuprofen
summary: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) effective for inflammation, toothache, menstrual cramps, and headaches.
uses: Musculoskeletal aches and sports sprains
Primary dysmenorrhea (menstrual cramps)
Dental discomfort and post-procedure swelling
Arthritic flare-ups
dosage: Adults: 200mg to 400mg every 6 to 8 hours with food or milk. Maximum OTC dosage: 1,200mg daily unless directed by physician.
sideEffects: Stomach irritation, heartburn, or acid reflux
Mild nausea
Risk of gastric ulceration with prolonged unmonitored use
precautions: Always take with or immediately after food to protect stomach lining
Contraindicated in individuals with active peptic ulcers, severe asthma, or kidney disease
Do not combine with other NSAIDs (such as Aspirin or Naproxen)
howItWorks: Reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), preventing the synthesis of pro-inflammatory prostaglandins.

name: Omeprazole
summary: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that decreases the amount of acid produced by the stomach lining.
uses: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and chronic heartburn
Gastric and duodenal ulcers
Protection against NSAID-induced gastric erosions
dosage: 20mg once daily taken 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast with a glass of water.
sideEffects: Headache
Abdominal pain or flatulence
Mild diarrhea or constipation
precautions: Swallow capsule whole; do not chew or crush the enteric-coated micro-granules
Not intended for instant relief of acute heartburn (takes 1-4 days for peak effect)
Long-term use requires monitoring of Vitamin B12 and magnesium levels
howItWorks: Permanently binds to and suppresses the hydrogen-potassium ATPase enzyme system ('proton pump') of gastric parietal cells.

name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
summary: A vital fat-soluble vitamin necessary for intestinal absorption of calcium, bone mineralization, and immune competence.
uses: Treatment and prevention of Vitamin D deficiency
Support for bone density and prevention of osteomalacia
Immune function support and muscle health
dosage: Deficiency treatment: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks with a fatty meal. Maintenance: 1,000-2,000 IU daily or as advised.
sideEffects: Very safe within normal dosing guidelines
Excessive mega-doses can cause hypercalcemia, thirst, or kidney stones
precautions: Consume with meals containing healthy dietary fats for optimal absorption
Check 25-hydroxy Vitamin D serum levels before and after long therapy cycles
howItWorks: Hydroxylated in the liver and kidneys to active calcitriol, which binds to vitamin D nuclear receptors to upregulate calcium-binding transport proteins.

name: Azithromycin
summary: A broad-spectrum macrolide antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections of the respiratory tract, ear, and skin.
uses: Bacterial sinusitis, pharyngitis, and tonsillitis
Community-acquired pneumonia and bronchitis
Bacterial ear infections and skin infections
dosage: Typically 500mg once daily for 3 to 5 days, taken strictly as prescribed by a licensed healthcare provider.
sideEffects: Mild diarrhea or stomach cramps
Nausea and transient vomiting
Temporary alteration in taste
precautions: Prescription strictly required — inappropriate use promotes bacterial resistance
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve early
Inform doctor if you have known cardiac arrhythmia (QT prolongation) or hepatic illness
howItWorks: Reversibly binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting transpeptidation and protein synthesis.
